name: Gridiron Air 777 scheme
description: All-white ex-Delta 777-200ER with two slate-grey cheatlines along the lower fuselage, a wider one under the windows and a thinner one below it, both pointed just behind the nose and dipping toward the tail cone; a small white 'GRIDIRON AIR' inside the upper line behind the forward door. Plain white fin, grey metal engine cowlings.

sources.title: Gridiron Air’ Boeing 777-232ER ‘N866DA’ @IND.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, AVA Navigate)
sources.note: 777-200ER N866DA, left side, taxiing at Indianapolis, 2026-02-01 (file description: 'Gridiron Air Boeing 777-232ER at IND from Houston'). Fitted to shapes/B77L.json (the 777-200 fuselage; door 1 pinned, camera slightly above): both cheatlines' edges, the title, engines and fin.

sources.title: FAA Order JO 7340.2M, Contractions (2023), three-letter designators
sources.note: RZN: GRIDIRON AIR LLC, United States, telephony REDZONE. Identifies the RZN callsign.

areas.name: upper (wider) slate cheatline, under the windows, pointed behind the nose and ending on the tail cone
lower (thinner) slate cheatline, pointed behind the nose and running off the belly under the tail

titles.style: Small plain capitals in white, inside the upper cheatline just behind the forward door (only about 25 cm tall: hardly visible beyond the gate).

notes: Gridiron Air is a US sports charter airline (FAA designator RZN, 'REDZONE'); its RZN 777-200 flights in Skyarium's log (2026-10-18…31) trace a college-football and South America charter pattern (EUG, LNK, MSN, PHX, SLC, MCO, LAX, EZE, GRU, SCL, FCO). Its 777-200ERs are ex-Delta (N860DA, N865DA, N866DA among the Commons categories naming Gridiron; only N866DA has a photo in Gridiron's paint). One left-side photo: the right side isn't seen (the title's place there is assumed the same, behind door 1), nor the belly. Measured on N866DA (2026-02-01): the upper cheatline runs about 0 to -0.45 m under the window line, the lower about -0.7 to -1.05 m, each about 0.4 m deep with a 0.3 m white gap, both pointed at x 0.02; the lower line runs off the belly at x 0.90-0.92, the upper ends on the tail cone at x 0.96. The cheatlines may be left over from the aircraft's earlier operator rather than a designed scheme; drawn as worn. Drawn on the 777F shape (B77L: the 777-200's fuselage, with windows where the -300ER's are); there is no 777-200ER shape. Gridiron's 737-800s weren't checked.
history: New in the LAX round 2 (2026-11-20); RZN had no scheme here before.
